Rashi on Chullin 12a:10:1.hebrew: לכי תיכול עלה כורא דמלחא - כשתמדוד לי כור של מלח בשכר שאומר לך, ובדיחותא בעלמא הוא:
Rashi on Chullin 12a:10:1.english: Go, eat a kor of salt with it - [Meaning:] When you measure out for me a kor of salt as payment for what I tell you. And this is merely said in jest.

Rashi on Chullin 12a:10:2.english: There is no presumption, etc. - Rather, it is a matter of doubt: perhaps he performs it, perhaps he does not perform it.

Rashi on Chullin 12a:10:3.english: Alternatively, [perhaps] a person heard, etc. - Meaning, even if a different person heard [him instruct the agent to slaughter].

Rashi on Chullin 12a:10:4.hebrew: תורם שלא מדעת אינה תרומה - דשליחות דתרומה מ"גם אתם" אתרבי (גיטין דף כג:) "אתם" "גם אתם" לרבות שלוחכם, ומינה: מה אתם לדעתכם אף שלוחכם לדעתכם:
Rashi on Chullin 12a:10:4.english: One who separates teruma without [the owner's] knowledge, it is not teruma - For the agency [that applies] to teruma is derived from [the extra word] "also you" (Gittin 23b): [the words] "you" [and] "also you" come to include your agent. And from this [we learn]: just as you [must separate teruma] with your knowledge, so too your agent [must separate it] with your knowledge.

Rashi on Chullin 12a:11:1.hebrew: דרך נבלות להשליך לאשפה - מדקאמר רבי נראין דברי ר' יהודה באשפה, מכלל דפליג רבי חנינא אפילו באשפה; ומדקאמר דברי ר' חנינא בבית, מכלל דפליג ר' יהודה אפילו בבית:
Rashi on Chullin 12a:11:1.english: It is normal for a carcass to be thrown into the garbage-dump - Since Rabbi says, "The words of R. Yehuda seem correct" [specifically] regarding a garbage-dump, this implies that R. Chanina disagrees even regarding a garbage-dump; and since he says "the words of R. Chanina [seem correct]" regarding a house, this implies that R. Yehuda disagrees even regarding a house.

Rashi on Chullin 12a:13:1.english: Everyone agrees that it is permitted - Because the majority of those commonly engaged in slaughtering are experts.

Rashi on Chullin 12a:13:2.hebrew: דאסור - דכיון דהשליכם שם, ודאי נתנבלה בשחיטתה, בשהייה או בדרסה:
Rashi on Chullin 12a:13:2.english: That it is prohibited - Since he threw them there, [the animal] certainly became an invalid carcass (neveilah) in the course of its slaughter, through a pause [in the cutting motion] or through pressing [the knife rather than drawing it].

Rashi on Chullin 12a:13:3.english: A person is not accustomed to throw his carcass into the garbage that is in the house - Because it rots and there is a foul smell.

Rashi on Chullin 12a:14:1.hebrew: והא אמרת דכולי עלמא וכו' - ומאי נראין דברי פלוני או דברי פלוני, והלא שניהם שוין בה:
Rashi on Chullin 12a:14:1.english: But did you not say that all [authorities agree], etc. - And what [sense is there in saying] "the words of so-and-so seem correct" or "the words of so-and-so," seeing that the two are equal in this [regard]?

Rashi on Chullin 12a:14:2.hebrew: אלא - פשיטא, באשפה דקתני היינו אשפה שבבית דפליגי בה, ואשמועינן דכרבי יהודה סבירא ליה:
Rashi on Chullin 12a:14:2.english: Rather - It is obvious that when it teaches "in a garbage heap," this means the garbage heap that is in the house, which is the subject of their dispute, and it teaches us that he [Rebbi] holds like Rabbi Yehuda.

Rashi on Chullin 12a:15:1.hebrew: הא אמרת לכולי עלמא שרי - ומאי נראין דברי רבי חנינא, דמשמע אבל דברי ר' יהודה אין נראין? ר' יהודה נמי שרי בה:
Rashi on Chullin 12a:15:1.english: But you said: Everyone permits it - Then what does [it mean that] "the words of Rabbi Chanina are correct," which implies that the words of Rabbi Yehuda are not correct? [That is not so -] Rabbi Yehuda also permits it in this case.

Rashi on Chullin 12a:15:2.hebrew: אלא פשיטא - מאי בית באשפה שבבית, ובה פליגי, ואשמועינן רבי דכרבי חנינא סבירא ליה:
Rashi on Chullin 12a:15:2.english: Rather, it is obvious - What is [meant by] "house"? [It means] the scrap heap that is in the house, and it is about this that they disagree, and it teaches us that Rabbi holds in accordance with Rabbi Ḥanina.

Rashi on Chullin 12a:15:3.hebrew: קשיא דרבי אדרבי - דברישא נראו לו דברי רבי יהודה דאסר באשפה שבבית, ובסיפא נראו לו דברי רבי חנינא בנו של רבי יוסי הגלילי דמתיר באשפה שבבית, אם כן קשיא דרבי אדרבי:
Rashi on Chullin 12a:15:3.english: There is a contradiction between [one statement of] Rebbi and [another statement of] Rebbi - For in the first clause, the words of Rabbi Yehuda, who prohibits [the found slaughtered bird] when it is in a garbage heap that is in the house, seemed correct to him; and in the last clause, the words of Rabbi Chanina son of Rabbi Yose HaGelili, who permits it when it is in a garbage heap that is in the house, seemed correct to him. If so, there is a contradiction between [one statement of] Rebbi and [another statement of] Rebbi.

Rashi on Chullin 12a:1:1.hebrew: פסח - דאמר רחמנא (שמות י״ב:ח׳) ואכלו את הבשר, ושלמים דאמר רחמנא (שם כט) ואכלו אותם אשר כופר בהם, מלמד שהכפרה תלויה אף באכילה. מאי איכא למימר? אלא ודאי אכיל, דסמיך ארובא היכא דלא אפשר, ואפי' הכי פליג בקטן וקטנה משום דאפשר. לדידן נמי היכי ילפינן מיניה? אלא ודאי הלכה למשה מסיני הא דסמכינן ארובא אפי' היכא דאפשר, אי נמי אחרי רבים להטות (שם כג) משמע בין רובא דאיתיה קמן בין רובא דליתיה קמן, דמאי שנא האי מהאי, ואהא מלתא סמכינן ולא בדקינן כל י"ח טרפות. ונקובת הריאה משום דשכיח בה ריעותא בדקינן, והיכא דאיתרמי דאיפרשה ריאה ולא בדק, מתאכלא, דסמכינן אהא ואדרב הונא דאמר (לעיל חולין דף ט.) נשחטה בחזקת היתר עומדת ואין מפרסמין הדבר:
Rashi on Chullin 12a:1:1.english: Pesach - For the Merciful One states (Exodus 12:8), "and they shall eat the flesh," and regarding peace-offerings the Merciful One states (ibid. 29), "and they shall eat those through whom atonement was achieved" - teaching that the atonement is dependent even on the eating. What is there to say? Rather, it certainly [assumes] that he eats [relying on the majority], for one relies on the majority [that the lung is unperforated] where it is not possible [to check it beforehand]; and even so, [the law] distinguishes in the case of a minor boy or girl, because for them it is possible [to check]. For us too - [in other cases] how do we derive [that one may rely on a majority] from this? Rather, it must be a halakha given to Moses at Sinai that we rely on a majority even where it is possible [to check]. Alternatively, [it is derived from] "one shall incline after the majority" (ibid. 23), which implies both a majority that is present before us and a majority that is not present before us - for what difference is there between the one and the other? And on this matter we rely, and do not check for all eighteen categories of tereifot. But a perforated lung - because a defect is common in it - we do check. And where it happened that the lung was set aside and not checked, it may nevertheless be eaten, since we rely on this [principle], and on Rav Huna, who said (above, Chullin 9a) that having been slaughtered, it retains its presumption of fitness, and we need not publicize the matter.

Rashi on Chullin 12a:3:1.english: If he knows that he is trained - [Meaning] that he recognizes him as one who is learned in the laws of slaughtering.

Rashi on Chullin 12a:3:2.hebrew: דידע דלא גמיר - שמכיר בו שאין יודע הלכות שחיטה:
Rashi on Chullin 12a:3:2.english: That he knows that [the other person] is not learned - He knows about him that he does not know the laws of slaughtering.

Rashi on Chullin 12a:3:3.hebrew: פשיטא - דראה מותר, דהא לא שהה ולא דרס, ולא ראה אסור, שמא שהה או דרס:
Rashi on Chullin 12a:3:3.english: Obvious - [If] he saw [him slaughter], it is permitted, since [he can testify] that he did not pause and did not press the knife; and [if] he did not see it, it is forbidden, lest he paused or pressed.

Rashi on Chullin 12a:4:1.english: Who does not know whether he has learned or has not learned [the laws of slaughtering] - This teaches us that we do not rely on an unspecified [slaughterer] unless [the observer] recognizes him as one who knows [these laws].

Rashi on Chullin 12a:6:1.hebrew: מומחין הן - שאם לא היה מומחה לא היה שוחט:
Rashi on Chullin 12a:6:1.english: They are experts - For if he were not an expert, he would not [know how to] slaughter.

Rashi on Chullin 12a:6:2.hebrew: רוב מצויין אצל שחיטה - כלומר, רוב השוחטין:
Rashi on Chullin 12a:6:2.english: Most of those who are found engaged in slaughter - That is to say, most slaughterers [are experts].

Rashi on Chullin 12a:8:2.english: And he found [produce] that had had teruma separated from it - And he did not know who had separated the teruma.

Rashi on Chullin 12a:9:1.english: There is a presumption that an agent fulfills his mission - All agents fulfill their mission, and we presume this of them, since they agreed to serve as agents.

Rashi on Chullin 12a:9:2.english: And if he does not fulfill his agency, then even with regard to slaughter also not - [Since] perhaps it was not his agent who did the slaughtering, but rather someone else who is not expert in the laws of ritual slaughter.

Tosafot on Chullin 12a:10:1.english: This is the correct version: "There is never a presumption that an agent, etc." - This is explained in the chapter Bekhol Me'arevin (Eruvin 32b).

Tosafot on Chullin 12a:11:1.hebrew: הרי שאבדו לו גדייו - ה"ה נגנבו, דמשום דחשיד אגנבה לא חשיד אנבלה; ובתוספתא קתני בהדיא: נגנבה לו תרנגולת ומצאה כו':
Tosafot on Chullin 12a:11:1.english: Behold, one whose goats were lost - The same is true if they were stolen, for since he is suspected of theft, he is not [thereby] suspected of [passing off] a carcass (neveilah). And in the Tosefta it teaches explicitly: "If a chicken was stolen from him and he found it, etc."

Tosafot on Chullin 12a:13:1.hebrew: כי פליגי באשפה שבבית - הוא הדין דפליגי בשוק בלא אשפה, כדמוכח באלו מציאות (ב"מ דף כד:), גבי ר' חנינא שמצא גדי שחוט בין טבריא לציפורי:
Tosafot on Chullin 12a:13:1.english: When they disagree, it is about a refuse-heap that is in a house - The same is true that they disagree [even in a case] in the marketplace without a refuse-heap, as is proven in [the chapter] Eilu Metzios (Bava Metzia 24b), regarding R. Chanina who found a slaughtered kid between Tiberias and Tzippori.

Tosafot on Chullin 12a:1:1.hebrew: פסח וקדשים מאי איכא למימר - מבשר תאוה לא פריך, משום דנראה דמדאורייתא לא חייש רבי מאיר למיעוטא אלא מדרבנן; ולהכי פריך הכי נמי, שמחמיר שלא לאכול בשר כלל, ואפילו מחמיר בשאר בשר, פסח וקדשים אין יכול להחמיר. ומדקדק, כי היכי דלר"מ יש חילוק מדרבנן בין אפשר ללא אפשר, ה"ה לרבנן:
Tosafot on Chullin 12a:1:1.english: Pesach and Kodashim (consecrated offerings), what is there to say? - Regarding ordinary meat (meat eaten for mere desire), [the Gemara] does not raise a difficulty, because it appears that biblically, Rabbi Meir is not concerned about the minority [of unskilled slaughterers], but only rabbinically. And therefore [regarding Pesach and Kodashim] it does raise the difficulty likewise: for [with ordinary meat,] one who is stringent not to eat meat at all - even though he is stringent regarding other meat [that is merely his own choice] - [but] regarding Pesach and Kodashim he cannot be stringent [and abstain from eating, since he is obligated to eat them]. And [the Gemara] infers precisely: just as, according to Rabbi Meir, there is a rabbinic distinction between where it is possible [to verify the slaughterer beforehand] and where it is not possible, so too the same applies according to the Rabbis [i.e., the majority view].

Tosafot on Chullin 12a:5:1.hebrew: או שאמר לשלוחו כו' - מעיקרא תנא מצא תרנגולת שחוטה בשוק, דאיכא למימר בעליה שחטוה; והדר אמר דאפי' אמר לשלוחו ומצאו השליח שהיא שחוטה, דהשתא שלא ברשות נשחטה, אפ"ה חזקתו שחוטה:
Tosafot on Chullin 12a:5:1.english: Or if he said to his agent, etc. - Initially [the baraita] taught [the case of] one who found a slaughtered chicken in the marketplace, where it can be said that its owner slaughtered it; and then it states that even if he told his agent [to slaughter it], and the agent found that it was [already] slaughtered - so that now it was slaughtered without [proper] authorization - even so, the presumption is that it was [validly] slaughtered.
